html:
SMTO-LLM-0020 — SMTO couldn't find a usable model at the model server

GUID: cc185660-0737-49a0-aa7b-6374b9be2b4e
Slug: model-unavailable
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • SMTO asked the model server which models it offers but got no usable list, or couldn't read the answer. SMTO won't quietly switch to another model, so the work can't start yet.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the model server is running and has finished loading a model. If SMTO runs it for you, open the Inference page and check that the model instance is running. A server that is still starting, or has no model loaded, offers no models to choose from.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. Also confirm the Endpoint is the right address. This shows whether SMTO is asking the right server and which model it finds there.
  3. If Auto-select model is on, turn it off, type the model's name in Model (or use Discover models), and select Save Main. With a named model, SMTO no longer depends on the server's model list to pick one.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model shows your model's name, and the task starts or continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model server. Don't point a stopped task at a different model to get past this; it must continue with the model it started with.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The required model could not be established: model discovery at the configured endpoint returned no usable model entries or an unreadable or oversized (over 4 MiB) /models response, or saved task preparation could not create a client for its recorded model; SMTO will not silently switch models (model_unavailable).

What this means

  • Model discovery or saved-profile preparation could not establish the required model selection; endpoint failure and an absent usable model list are different possibilities. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Model discovery or saved-profile preparation could not establish the required model selection; endpoint failure and an absent usable model list are different possibilities.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the saved model identity, configured endpoint and model-list result separately; a discovery transport failure does not prove the weights were removed.

How to fix it

  • Request the endpoint's /models with the configured API key and confirm it returns a non-empty data list under 4 MiB. Load or serve the intended model, or turn off Auto-select model and set an explicit model on the role in Settings › Setup › Model routing (explicit names don't depend on the listing). For a task-preparation failure, restore the role and endpoint that serve the task's recorded model; saved runs must continue with their recorded model.
  • Restore the saved model at the configured endpoint before resuming. Verify Mission Control → Model Configuration → LLM endpoint URL.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open LLM Endpoint: model-configuration / llm_base_url. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Preparation accepts the intended model while preserving the saved task identity.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
